hypotheses.claim: The ZM zone clamp is real server-side: a ZM calling /api/dashboard/action-required?zoneId=<other> still gets only their own zone, and CSM/OH genuinely receive all zones — so C9's lens is a data lens, not just a layout lens.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: the clamp only covers action-required; critical-queue / company-plant-overview take scope but never narrow it, so a ZM sees cross-zone rows
hypotheses.altCheck: sed -n '803,930p' apps/backend/src/dashboard/dashboard.service.ts — actionRequiredZone() clamps at :912, but criticalQueue(scope) at :803 takes scope with no visible zoneId argument; cannot confirm the SQL filter from the read

hypotheses.claim: There is no assign-from-dashboard path in the product at all: the critical-queue rows have no consumer that can dispatch, so DASH-G01 is COMPLETE work, not a re-mount of an existing widget.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: the Scheduler Console / Today's Dispatch already renders a grouped assignable queue over the same aggregation, making the dashboard queue a duplicate rather than a gap
hypotheses.altCheck: grep -rn 'apiZoneEngineers|CriticalQueueGroup' apps/admin/src — apiZoneEngineers imported from api/schedules into ManagerDashboard.tsx:15 and passed to nothing; CriticalQueueGroup only typed in api/dashboard.ts, ManagerDashboard, ZmDashboard, CentralDashboard, EscalationQueueList

hypotheses.claim: The seven CARD_DESTINATION routes are actually reachable by a Zonal Manager, so wiring the dashboard panel to that existing map (DASH-G02) genuinely lands the ZM on a working page rather than a role-blocked one.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: some destinations (/verification, /intraday, /component-requests) are gated to CSM/OH, so the same map wired onto a ZM dashboard produces dead links for the very persona that needs them
hypotheses.altCheck: grep -rn 'ActionRequiredPanel' apps/admin/src --include=*.tsx — the panel is mounted ONLY in ZmDashboard.tsx:129 (ZM-facing), while the map it would borrow lives in the Scheduler Console, a surface a ZM may not reach; route-level role guards in AppRoutes.tsx are not resolvable statically

hypotheses.claim: The five unwired Action Required card keys have no counting source anywhere in the backend, so DASH-G05 is five new aggregations rather than five wire-ups.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: the owning modules (Issue 11 batches, 21 component-blocked, 29 insertions, 30 manual assignment, 35 non-op) already expose count endpoints and only the dashboard fan-in is missing
